review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the directory for simp attributes and uses of the floating-coordinate API. There are no @[simp] declarations anywhere in the directory. mem_floatingCoordinates is used via rw at lines 57, 97, 280, 284 and 344, and via .mp/.mpr at lines 271 and 282. I did not run Lean, so I did not check whether the suggested attribute changes any existing simp call. The unfolding simp only [floatingDegree] calls are local and fine, and I made no claim about them.

findings.excerpt:
lemma mem_floatingCoordinates {x : Fin N → ℚ} {i : Fin N} :
    i ∈ floatingCoordinates x ↔ 0 < x i ∧ x i < 1 := by
  simp [floatingCoordinates]
findings.problem: floatingCoordinates is a plain def (a Finset.filter), and its membership lemma is not a simp lemma. Simp therefore cannot see through `i ∈ floatingCoordinates x` unless the definition is unfolded by hand. The file works around this with manual `rw [mem_floatingCoordinates]` at lines 57, 97, 280, 284 and 344, and with `.mp`/`.mpr` at lines 271 and 282. Membership in this set is the canonical normal form `0 < x i ∧ x i < 1`, and every use wants that rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. This is the standard orientation for a mem lemma and cannot loop, because the right-hand side contains no floatingCoordinates. The `rw [mem_floatingCoordinates]` steps could then be dropped or replaced by `simp`. Examples are `simp only [mem_floatingCoordinates]`, or the `rcases ... <;> simp [h]` goals at lines 284–285 and 344–345. A convenient version would also have the `hiF` hypotheses in `exists_rounding_step` and `exists_rounding_induction` simp straight to bounds. A parallel `@[simp] mem_filter`-style lemma for `floatingDegree` is unnecessary, because it is a card of a filter.
findings.benefit: Callers of the API get the canonical bounds form from `simp` without knowing to unfold `floatingCoordinates`. The proofs stop repeating manual rewrites. This matches the Mathlib convention that mem lemmas for filter-defined finsets are simp, as with Finset.mem_filter.
